   STAFF REPORT

 Meeting Date:  February 27, 2025
 To:  Recreation and Parks Council Liaisons Councilmembers John
  Mirisch and Mary Wells
 From:  Michael Muse, Recreation Services Manager
  Patty Acuña, Assistant Director of Community Services
 Subject:  Recommendations for the Finalization of the Pickleball Pilot
  Program

INTRODUCTION
On January 12, 2020, the City of Beverly Hills Community Services Department kicked off
a pickleball pilot program to gauge interest from the community. Two tennis courts (courts
13 & 14), on the north/west, lower level of the facility were converted into 8 pickleball
courts at the La Cienega Tennis Center and one tennis court (court 1) at Roxbury Park
was converted into 4 pickleball courts. Due to the Covid-19 pandemic and shelter in place
orders the pickleball program was immediately paused. As facilities began to open back
up to the public in 2021, pickleball along with tennis resumed. In March of 2021 the Pilot
program was able to resume once all Covid-19 related restrictions and the emergency
orders were lifted utilizing all 12 courts. Between April of 2023 and November 2024, staff
presented data and community feedback to the Recreation and Parks Commission
resulting in a recommendation to conclude the pickleball pilot program and institute a
permanent pickleball program.

DISCUSSION
The pickleball pilot program initially launched with converting tennis courts 13 and 14 at
the La Cienega Tennis Center and court 1 at Roxbury Park into pickleball courts. The
lines for pickleball were overlayed on the existing tennis lines to create a total of 12 total
pickleball courts. Portable pickleball nets were purchased and set-up and broken down
daily for designated pickleball play time. The program hours were Mondays, Tuesdays
and Fridays, 11am – 3pm, Thursdays 6pm – 10pm and Sundays, 9am – 12pm. As
demand for pickleball court time increased, the City expanded pickleball court times at
both La Cienega Tennis Center and Roxbury Tennis Center. The times were changed to
7am – 10pm Monday through Sunday.

By the end of 2022 after program hours were increased to full days, staff began to receive
complaints regarding the noise levels generated from pickleball play at the La Cienega
Center. While one tennis court allows for 2 to 4 players per reservation maximum,
 February 27, 2025
pickleball allows for a maximum of 4 players playing at a time, however often there are
more than four as people prefer to round robin or to sub players in. This will often provide
for 6-8 people on a court, however only four playing at any one time. Pickleball at minimum
will allow for 16 players on one tennis court at a time playing. The noise came from an
increase in players on each court and the sound of the plastic pickleball striking the plastic
paddle which was reported to be overwhelmingly loud.

The Recreation & Parks Commission were provided updates on community feedback and
established an Ad Hoc to discuss ideas on how to address the above concerns. In addition
to the noise concerns the Ad Hoc and Commission were looking at ways to address the
feedback that the portable nets purchased were not withstanding the high recurrence of
play and the dislike of the court configuration.

The direction from the Recreation & Parks Commission in April 2022 was to move to a
phase 2 of the pilot program that would address concerns of noise, court configuration
and size and nets. Phase 2 of the pilot program began in June of 2022. The courts were
reconfigured to the opposite side of the La Cienega Tennis Center facility to court 1
(grandstand court) and court 8 located on the east side of the facility. Staff also purchased
higher quality temporary nets. The conversion of court 1 from tennis to pickleball seemed
to be an excellent option for pickleball players due to the increased size of the back court.
All tennis courts with the exception of court 1 have minimal back court space. However, it
was not well received by the tennis community due to court 1 being the preferred court for
ball machine use, and tournament play.

In early 2024, Recreation & Parks Commission requested that the pickleball data be
presented to the commission to begin the process of finalizing the pickleball pilot program.
The Recreation & Parks Ad Hoc Committee which included Commissioner Amie Sherry
and JR Dzubak met several times to review a variety of program components and
operational needs. Staff presented several updates on statistics of how both tennis and
pickleball usage had increased and feedback from various users on the phase 2
reconfiguration of courts both in support and opposition.

Concerns brought forward to department staff and commissioners about noise impacts
from tennis players as well as neighbors along Le Deux which is directly across from court
1. The current court configuration specifically use of court 1 was ideal to pickleball players
due to the space of the larger court. It was being requested that this court remain and
become permanent.

As staff was preparing to bring forward recommendations for the permanent program
including the configuration of courts, a sound study was conducted. Staff worked with a
third-party vendor to conduct a noise study for both La Cienega Tennis Center and
Roxbury Tennis Center to test the court configurations in response to the noise concerns.

Staff continued to receive complaints and comparisons to other facilities regarding the
reservation system used for court bookings. Staff began to conduct research regarding a
new reservation software specifically for tennis and pickleball. The software would provide
easy access to tennis/pickleball users to make reservations, cancel reservations and allow
players to check in when arriving at this facility. This software will allow a new feature to
be implemented that would require each person register and pay an individual player fee
versus a court fee.

At the August 27, 2024, Recreation and Parks Commission meeting staff presented a
complete evaluation of the pilot program. The evaluation from staff showed that usage of
the tennis courts between January through May of 2023 to January through May of 2024
grew by 13.30% and pickleball court usage grew by 15.81% during that same period of

time. The evaluation also demonstrated that between January through May of 2023 to
January through May of 2024 revenue for tennis increased by 45% and for pickleball
increased by 44%. At this meeting, over 30 public comments were made to the
commission in support of moving pickleball out of the pilot phase and into a permanent
program. The request to the staff and commission was to also consider adding additional
courts, purchasing permanent nets and restriping the courts with permanent pickleball
lines. While majority of the public comments at this meeting were in favor of the program,
there were a few in attendance that were opposed to dedicating courts to pickleball
because of the noise disruption as well as reducing the ability to reserve tennis courts.

At the November 26, 2024, Recreation & Parks Commission meeting, staff presented the
noise study results from the vendor from both facilities. The noise study found that the
noise level at Roxbury Park did exceed the Los Angeles County’s noise standard, however
with the ambient noise from Olympic Boulevard concluded that the current pickleball noise
level and court configuration would have little effect on the overall noise. The study found
that the noise level on court 1 at the La Cienega Tennis Center did exceed the County’s
noise standard but did not exceed the standard at court 8.

Additionally, the study found that the noise emanating from court 8 was so minimal that
additional pickleball courts would not exceed the county standard. This is due to the
pickleball noise blending with the ambient noise from La Cienega Boulevard and the
distance of court 8 and the presence of tennis courts between the residents on Le Doux
Road.

Following the information provided by staff regarding the noise study and hearing the
recommendations from the Ad Hoc to establish a permanent pickleball program the
commission approved in a 4-1 vote to recommend that the pickleball pilot program be
finalized. The recommendations for the permanent program are as follows:

Court Configurations:
- Roxbury Tennis Center:
  o Maintain court 1 as a dedicated pickleball court.
  o No additional courts recommended
-  La Cienega Tennis Center:
  o Revert court 1 to tennis
  o Convert court, 8 & 12 to pickleball
  o Recommend an additional tennis court (court 7) be converted to a dedicated
  pickleball court on the east side of the tennis facility.

-  Each court be restriped with permanent pickleball lines.
-  Purchase and install permanent pickleball nets.
-  Implement a new registration software to facilitate court reservations.

FISCAL IMPACT
Total estimated annual expense for equipment and software related to the Pickleball
Program is $25,600. Based on the pilot program, it is anticipated that nets will need to be
replaced with an annual cost of $6,400. Additionally, the cost for purchase and use of a
reservation software system, Playbypoint would be $9,599.88 per year per site (Roxbury
and La Cienega) for a total annual cost of $19,200. The City has negotiated a 5-year
agreement for a total not to exceed $95,998.80, the ongoing cost would be requested
through the budget process. This excludes credit card processing fees which are set for
by third party processor, CardConnect at 2.7% + 15 cents per transaction.

The one-time cost associated with the reconfiguration of courts is estimated at $99,360
The tennis courts for both Roxbury and the La Cienega Tennis Center are traditionally
scheduled to be resurfaced every 5 years. Once the courts are converted, they will be
added to the ongoing resurfacing schedule through CIP 00483.

There is an anticipated increase in revenue once the program changes are implemented
due to the proposed implementation of a new fee structure introducing a per player fee.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff is seeking direction from the Recreation & Parks Council Liaisons on the next steps
with the pickleball pilot program.
- Complete the pilot program and transition into a permanent program.
- Approve the court configurations presented in this report
- Approval to purchase equipment including a reservation software
